evidence.quote: Let $M$ be a closed connected smooth four-manifold, let $0<T<\infty$, and let $g(t)$, $0\le t<T$, be a smooth Ricci flow with smooth initial metric.

exclusions.query: scalar curvature extension in dimensions other than four
exclusions.reason: The theorem is stated only for closed four-manifolds.

prerequisites.concept: smooth extension of four-dimensional Ricci flow under scalar bound

outputs.exact_statement: Let $M$ be a closed connected smooth four-manifold, let $0<T<\infty$, and let $g(t)$, $0\le t<T$, be a smooth Ricci flow with smooth initial metric. If $$\sup_{M\times[0,T)}|R(g(t))|<\infty,$$ then there are $\varepsilon>0$ and a smooth Ricci flow $\widetilde g(t)$ on $M$, $0\le t<T+\varepsilon$, such that $\widetilde g(t)=g(t)$ for every $t<T$.
If a Ricci flow on a closed smooth four-manifold has finite maximal smooth existence time $T$, then $$\limsup_{t\uparrow T}\max_{x\in M}R(g(t))(x)=+\infty.$$

The functional in Equation [eq:energy-functional] is defined on the preceding metrics. For a variation with the same root decay, $$DE_g(\dot g)=\int\left\langle\tfrac12R(g)g-\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}(g),\dot g\right\rangle_g \,d\mu_g. \label{ell:first-variation}$$ It is invariant under diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity whose root displacement, including scaled derivatives throughout the isotopy, is $O(r^{1-q'})$ for some $q'>1$. A global length scaling by $s$, accompanied by a coordinate dilation at infinity restoring the leading tensor $\delta$, multiplies $E$ by $s^2$. Under Equation [eq:tree-ricci-error], $|E(g)|\le CM$.

For the fixed tree and the sequences just specified, $$E(g)=o(M).
 \label{ell:little-oh}$$ For $M=0$ the assertion means $E(g)=0$.

For a sufficiently small cap and all sufficiently late times, the following conclusions hold.* **Scale and energy bounds.* One has $$\begin{aligned} cr^4\leq\mathop{\mathrm{Vol}}_t B_t(x,r)&\leq Cr^4, &\int_M|\mathop{\mathrm{Rm}}|^2\,d\mu_t&\leq C,\label{geom:volume-energy}\\ |\nabla^k\mathop{\mathrm{Rm}}|(x,t)&\leq C_k l(x,t)^{-2-k}, &|\nabla^k\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}|(x,t)&\leq C_k l(x,t)^{-1-k}. \label{eq:ricci-improvement} \end{aligned}$$ Here $07 below.

Suppose annular regions have inner and outer radii $r_-\ll r_+$ and every escaping intermediate annulus converges smoothly to a round flat quotient annulus. Assume for some $\sigma>0$ and all needed finite orders that $$r^2|\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}|_{k+2,r}\leq
 C\big((r/r_+)^\sigma+(r_-/r)^\sigma\big).$$ Fix $0<\mu<\min(1,\sigma)$. After removing fixed-factor boundary collars, for this fixed exponent, $$\label{eq:neck-decay}
 r^2|\mathop{\mathrm{Rm}}|_{k,r}\leq
 C\big((r/r_+)^\mu+(r_-/r)^\mu\big).$$ A single equivariant coordinate system on a shortened neck gives the same bound for $g-\delta$, with scaled derivatives. Infinite half-necks are allowed. One may also use slowly varying coefficients on the boundary terms, when the forcing and boundary data obey their corresponding bounds.

Let $h_i\to0$ and let $J_i$ be time intervals of length $\delta_i=o(h_i)$ tending to $T$. Distances initially of order $O(h_i)$ change by $o(h_i)$ throughout $J_i$. If a material point has $l\geq c h_i$ at one time, it has $l\geq c' h_i$ throughout (after extraction for a sequential assertion). Regular compact charts at this scale persist, and their scaled metric coefficients, with any fixed finite number of scaled derivatives, change by $O(\delta_i/h_i)$ in fixed material coordinates.
Fix $u>0$. Let $s_i<t_i<T$ tend to $T$, where $t_i$ is the first time after $s_i$ for which $|\log(a(t_i)/a(s_i))|=u$. Then $$\frac{t_i-s_i}{a(s_i)^2}\longrightarrow\infty.$$

If a concentration point exists, there are parabolically rescaled intervals $I=[-\theta,1+\theta]$, for one fixed $\theta>0$, with physical squared length units $d_i\to0$, such that the root scale throughout $I$ is comparable to a number $a_i\to0$ and changes by a fixed factor between $0$ and $1$. Put $\epsilon_i=\sqrt{d_i}$. In these units $$|R|\leq C\epsilon_i^2,\qquad
 |\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}|_{k,r}\leq C_k\epsilon_i/r$$ at regularity scales $r$ in a bounded range. For $a_i\ll r\lesssim1$ the cluster has flat quotient annular limits with nontrivial group. At any fixed time, allowable root centers differ by $O(a_i)$.

On the intervals of Proposition 12, geometry at length $h\lesssim1$ moves negligibly over windows $\Delta t$ satisfying $\epsilon_i\Delta t/h\to0$. Regular chart coefficients change by $O(\epsilon_i\Delta t/h)$ with every fixed number of scaled derivatives. At $h\asymp a_i$, old and new centers are $O(a_i)$ apart; at $a_i\ll h\lesssim1$ they are $o(h)$ apart.

Suppose $PZ=Z$, $Z$ is compactly supported in time, and $E=(\partial_\tau-\Delta_\delta)Z$. For $1<p\le2$, set $$z(s)=\left\|\,\|Z(s,\cdot,\tau)\|_{L^2(S^3)}\,\right\|_{L^p_\tau}.$$ With either ordinary or constant-normalized time measure, $$\mathcal Lz:=-z''-\frac3s z'+\frac3{s^2}z
 \le\left\|\,\|E(s,\cdot,\tau)\|_{L^2(S^3)}\,\right\|_{L^p_\tau}.
 \label{para:radial-inequality}$$ For $p=2$ the same conclusion holds for a Hilbert direct sum of fields in different charts or time windows with the same radial variable. The homogeneous comparison powers are $s$ and $s^{-3}$.

Let $T$ be a spatially constant multiple of $\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}$ on an annulus whose metric has scaled $C^{j+1}$ distance at most $e$ from $\delta$. On a fixed-width shell of radius $s$ in its Cartesian coordinates, $$\sum_{k=1}^j s^k|\nabla^kT|
 \le C_j\left(\sum_{k=1}^j s^k\sup|D^kPT|
              +e\sup|T|_{j,s}\right),
 \label{para:mean-derivatives}$$ where the suprema on the right use a fixed enlargement of the shell.

There are fixed $N_0\gg1$, $r_0>0$, and $0<\alpha<\min(\mu,1)$, and a choice of $N_1$ in Equation [eq:root-energy], such that $$\begin{aligned} V(r)&\le C\left[(a/r)^{2+\alpha}K +\widetilde\delta_i\bigl((a/r)^\alpha+r^\alpha\bigr)\right], \label{para:exterior-v}\\ A(r)&\le C\left[(a/r)^{2+\alpha}K+\widetilde\delta_i\right] \label{para:exterior-a} \end{aligned}$$ for $N_0a\le r\le r_0$, where $\widetilde\delta_i\to0$ and $\widetilde\delta_i\ge\epsilon$. The constants are independent of $i$ and $r$.

For every fixed $D_1$, $$\|H_*\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C_{D_1,p}(K+o_i(1)).
 \label{eq:maximal-ricci}$$

Take any sequence of times with $\eta(t) e0$ and extract a tree as in Theorem 6. On its true compact and half-neck pieces in $B_t(x_t,D_0a)$, let $r$ be the physical length of the local regular patch, in $I$-units. For every fixed required derivative order $j$ there are $C, u>0$ such that $$(r/a)^2|G|_{j,r}(t) \le C igl(H_*(t)+\epsilon igr)e^{- u D}. \label{eq:interior-weighted}$$ Here $D=0$ on compact pieces, including truncated outer compact regions. On a joining neck $D$, up to bounded shifts, is the minimum of the logarithmic distances from the two ends. It is the half-neck coordinate used in Section 2. Constants may depend on the extracted tree, and the exponent may be decreased.

Let $G(x)=c_4|x|^{-2}$ be the fundamental solution for the chosen sign of the Euclidean Laplacian. For $0<q<2$, its Newton operator is bounded $$\Delta^{-1}:H^{k-2}_{q+2}(\mathbb{R}^4)\longrightarrow H^k_q(\mathbb{R}^4).$$ For $1<q<2$, if $h\in H^{k-3}_{q+3}(\mathbb{R}^4)$ and $\int_{\mathbb{R}^4}h=0$ componentwise, then $$\|\Delta^{-1}h\|_{H^{k-1}_{q+1}}
             \le C\|h\|_{H^{k-3}_{q+3}}.
 \label{collar:zero-mass-newton}$$ Finally, on an annulus or ball of outer radius comparable to $R$, if $\Delta W=H$, boundary strips control $W$ in scaled $H^{k-2}$ by $b_0$, and $c_r=r^2\|H\|_{H^{k-4}(r)}$, then $$\sup_r\|W\|_{H^{k-2}(r)}\le C\left(b_0+\sum_rc_r\right).
 \label{collar:green-sum}$$ The constant is independent of the number of shells. A filled ball has no inner boundary term; its innermost shell is replaced by a fixed ball.

Choose sufficiently small $\sigma_0>0$ and sufficiently large fixed $N$. At a time near $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\eta$, choose an exterior annular chart at scale $b$ with domain, in collar units, $\{1/8<|x|<16\}/\Gamma$, retaining slightly larger boundary margins when necessary. Keep its map into the material manifold and its group fixed. For all sufficiently late $i$, throughout any interval on which its metric stays within $\sigma_0$ of the flat metric through the required fixed derivative order, the following assertions hold. Every closed shortened collar lies at distance comparable to $b$ from the current center $x_t$; its middle bands cover the corresponding shortened distance annuli. The component on the designated inner side of a middle sphere contains $B_t(x_t,N_1a)$ and is contained in $B_t(x_t,Cb)$, with fixed constants.

For the preceding extensions and partition, $$\label{eq:variation-lower}
 \sum_j\int_I\eta^2\chi_j E_j'\,dt
 \ge 2a^4K^2-a^4\bigl[CN^{-2\alpha}K^2
                              +o_i(1)(K+1)^2\bigr].$$
Along the buffered intervals, $K_i\to0$.

There is a single set of material points $\mathcal G_i$, independent of time, whose complement has volume $o(a_i^4)$, which is $o(a_i)$-dense at every $t\in[0,1]$ in a smaller neighborhood of the cluster. For points $x,y\in\mathcal G_i$ in that neighborhood whose distance at either endpoint is at most $Ca_i$, $$\label{final:good-distance}
 |d_1(x,y)-d_0(x,y)|=o(a_i),$$ uniformly for each fixed $C$.
Let $\mathfrak a_i(t)$ denote the root scale of Proposition 8, computed in interval units. Then $$a_i^{-1}\bigl|\mathfrak a_i(1)-\mathfrak a_i(0)\bigr| \longrightarrow0.$$
